title: My AI's performance so far this year
author: SnowSilent7695
selftext:
Late last year, I decided to built a platform that ingested, cleaned and curated data from a variety of different domains (market data, fundamentals, transcripts, news, macro, estimates, etc.) to let frontier models build portfolios that could beat the market. While it took longer than expected, I finally launched at the end of April and figured I share the results so far. Currently four strategies are employed: momentum, value, small-mid cap, and a blend of fundamentals and momentum.  Here are the results so far

|Value|\+17.3%|20|\+11.0%|
|Momentum/Fundamentals|\+7.2%|10|\-3.1%|

comments.author: Unfair_Set_355
comments.body: Nice breakdown. The gap between your small/mid cap sleeve and the momentum/fundamentals blend says a lot, strategy selection seems to matter more than "AI vs not AI" here. I've been building something similar (an agent I build on Raijin) and honestly the biggest improvement wasn't a smarter model, it was closing the gap between backtest and realized performance. Logging slippage and actual fill quality made a bigger difference than I expected. How are you tracking realized vs theoretical returns on your end, or is it still early enough that you're mostly going off the backtest numbers?

comments.author: PatientArtichoke3843
comments.body:
Congrats on shipping, the data plumbing part always takes 3x longer than the model part. Two months is a fun start but honestly too short to tell you much yet, especially for the momentum sleeve. If the market's been trending, a momentum book can look great on pure beta, so the question I'd be asking is what each strategy looks like against its own factor benchmark rather than against SPY or zero. Value vs a value ETF, momentum vs MTUM, that kind of thing. That comparison is brutal but it's the only one that tells you the model is actually adding something.



 I built something in the same space, open source Claude Code skill plus the data and execution layers underneath, so grain of salt since I'm the dev. The piece that ended up mattering most wasn't the strategies, it was a scorecard that grades every call against forward returns and alpha vs benchmark over time. Watching your own hit rate get measured is humbling and it kills a lot of stories you'd otherwise tell yourself. [https://github.com/pedrobraiti/vizier-trading-skill](https://github.com/pedrobraiti/vizier-trading-skill) if you're curious.



 Also genuinely curious, how much of the result do you attribute to the curated data vs the frontier model itself? My hunch from building the data side is that clean timestamped data does more of the work than people give it credit for.
